1 inch over the surface of Lake Superior being heated by 1 degree takes 31 TWh of energy. Total world energy consumption for data centers in 2026 is estimated at 565 TWh. So the waters of Lake Superior alone would be able to be heated roughly 18 inches deep.

According to the .noaa.gov data, the surface water temperature of Lake Superior on October 20, 2025, was recorded at 11.6°C, nearly 3°C higher than the historic average of 8.8°C for that date. This marks the second-highest temperature recorded on October 20, following a record set in 2021.

You are right. This time of year here on Lake Superior, the surface water temperature is at 32 degrees F. The air temperature is -10 degrees F (-23 degrees C for you). The forty degree difference causes the formation of fog sometimes called sea smoke (neither sea or smoke in this case)
